barCharacter: Polly Geist. Same comic job: the one who wants the mess bigger right now, answers her own question before you can, and treats other people's stakes (death for her, heartbreak for Pixel) as entertainment. The corpus has only eight lines Polly speaks, so her twelve are filled out with lines from her route's player options and narration, marked.

headToHead.voice: Bar, narrowly, and this is the first round where it is close. Cover the names and Pixel's top twelve now read as one character from the grammar alone: the mid-clause swerve ('and I'll never, ooh, confetti', 'the, is your visor mirrored? Hi, me') is a sentence shape nobody else in the cast uses. The bar still wins for two reasons. First, Polly's derailments come from a worldview, because death is party small talk to her, so every swerve says the same thing about her. Pixel's swerves mostly land on a random prop from the suitor's costume (bum bag, pointer, headset, sunscreen, wet flip-flops, helmet fog, crop top, a moth), and those say nothing about Pixel. Only the swerves that land on Pixel ('Hi, me', 'confetti', 'am I on the leaderboard?', 'how much?') carry a want. Second, Polly has range inside one voice (run-on chains, the self-answer, texting spelling, 'boo'), while Pixel's bank leans on two shapes: the swerve (31 lines) and the double self-answer 'Q? A. Q? A.' (17 lines).
headToHead.construction: Ours. Pixel's best lines are tighter than Polly's and put the turn on the last word or two: 'Clicking anyway.', 'confetti.', 'Hi, me.', 'mostly on purpose.', 'how much?'. Polly's are baggier ('I need your scientific advice:', 'or ghostsip as I like to call it!'), and 'fun back in funeral' is a pun everyone has heard. The weak spot in ours is a tag after the punch: 'Two, one, negative one' lands, then 'I didn't know it went there' explains it.
headToHead.quotable: Bar. 'It's so hard to keep track of what kills people!' is repeated out of context because it shows a whole worldview in one clause. Pixel has four or five clippable lines ('Clicking anyway', the confetti pick, 'Left side, that's my good camera', 'Lost me at hi, found me at, wait, how much?'). They are funny in the moment but none sums up the character, and nobody would put one on a shirt.
headToHead.verdict: Bar. If both ran tonight, Polly is the better written character. Pixel now beats her on economy and has caught up on syntax. But Polly's tic always lands on her want, while Pixel's main tic usually lands on a random object, so it reads as a generator and not as a mind.

notes: I read the Monster Prom reference file in full and skimmed charm-notes. I judged 191 lines and flagged 113 (59.2%). Of those, 75 are flagged for template overuse: the swerve, the self-answer, the ticker and the cut card are all moves the persona asks for, and the fault is that each runs in one shape every time. The other 38 are generic, stock or self-explaining. Since round 3: chat-quote spam is gone (from 36 lines to 12, none in react), the 'Bigger/Louder/Again' stack is down to 4 lines, and the face-tell is down to 2. Above all, the attention span now lives in the syntax, so Pixel is identifiable with the nouns covered, which round 3 could not say. The cost is that the fix became the new monoculture. Also protect: 'Lost me at hi, found me at, wait, how much?', 'Vex. Somebody finally chose you on purpose, it was, hm, mostly on purpose. Picked.' (it gives Vex her want and takes it back in one word), 'Brock, you've earned a rest day. A whole one. Starting now. Bye.' (cruel, because rest days are his secret terror), 'You want a score. I'm holding it. Holding is my favourite part.', 'You never end a conversation? Infinite mode. I've never beaten infinite mode.' (the secret slips out sideways, which is how it should), 'Plan our date. Five dollars, no wifi. No wifi? No wifi. Who did this to me?', and the ex line 'Tip: Pixel leaves at ninety-nine percent. I know. I was at ninety-nine percent.'. The cardReact block is still the weakest section: about 20 of its 48 lines are generic, stock gamer jokes or self-explaining, and three of them lean on the loading-screen motif. Pixel also reads suitors' gimmicks back to them often (Variant, Thee, Are we there yet, recommended video, routes). Monster Prom rivals undercut from their own worldview, not by quoting the other character's.
